title: apg projects model + node-file serialization
goal: Ship the first-class project concept (mutation guard, worktree/branch contexts, init version gate) and the 2.0 node-file serialization model ("serialize nodes, not specs"), bootstrapped via dogfooding.

name: change-sets
body: 2.0-mapping: the projects model domain — a project is a container for a change-set over the graph (and the code underpinning it); a project ≠ spec ≠ plan, it contains those things (SPEC-apg-projects.md §1.1, §2). Old-model Domain node for the whole change-set `apg-projects`: the worktree/branch context, the membership guard, node-file serialization semantics, and the .trans plan bridge all express this one domain concept.

name: apg-cli
body: 2.0-mapping: the apg binary itself (§2.3 "the binary", §6 agent flow) — the single C4 system that hosts the project commands, the mutation guard, the layers serializer, the plan bridge and the init/version gate. All five containers are proposed tier-3 nodes (pending anchors) — their code does not exist in the v0.10.4 graph except where a container maps onto an existing function (mutation-guard → apg.artifacts.write_jsonl_and_reingest).

name: ProjectStarted
body: 2.0-mapping: source §2.1 — `apg project start <name>` creates the project context: worktree + branch + auto-scan branch DB in one command; the event a change-set comes into being. 2.0 models events as Entity kind=event; the old model has no kind field, so this maps to a DomainEvent node.

name: NodeFileWritten
body: 2.0-mapping: source §4.2 — every node/edge mutation writes its file(s) and auto-commits on the project branch (one commit per mutation, single-file diffs); the event a node file lands in the worktree. 2.0: Entity kind=event; old model: DomainEvent node.

name: MutationRequiresProject
body: 2.0 source §2.2: "It is not possible to mutate the graph without a project — at all." Writes refuse outside a project context — the durable node/edge mutations (`apg node`/`apg edge`; the old spec/invariant/note writes are node/edge mutations here) and the transient plan/review mutations; membership = the project's worktree on the project's branch. Materialized as an old-model DomainRule (product Invariant auto-created).

body: 2.0 source §2.2: "It is not possible to mutate the graph without a project — at all." Writes refuse outside a project context — the durable node/edge mutations (`apg node`/`apg edge`; the old spec/invariant/note writes are node/edge mutations here) and the transient plan/review mutations; membership = the project's worktree on the project's branch. name: PairwiseEdgeMatching
body: 2.0 source §4.1: an edge appears in both endpoint files (out in the source's, in in the target's); an in/out edge in one file without the matching out/in edge in the other endpoint's file is an error caught at ingestion; outgoing edges are canonical. Materialized as an old-model DomainRule (product Invariant auto-created).

title: PairwiseEdgeMatching
body: 2.0 source §4.1: an edge appears in both endpoint files (out in the source's, in in the target's); an in/out edge in one file without the matching out/in edge in the other endpoint's file is an error caught at ingestion; outgoing edges are canonical. Materialized as an old-model DomainRule (product Invariant auto-created).

name: PlanCoversSolution
body: 2.0 source §5: every solution node's implemented-by FQN must be touched by at least one plan task; the bridge is complete iff coverage holds. The plan is the HOW for the whole solution. Materialized as an old-model DomainRule (product Invariant auto-created).

title: PlanCoversSolution
body: 2.0 source §5: every solution node's implemented-by FQN must be touched by at least one plan task; the bridge is complete iff coverage holds. The plan is the HOW for the whole solution. Materialized as an old-model DomainRule (product Invariant auto-created).

name: DriftIsError
body: 2.0 source §4.1: an implemented-by code FQN that is gone from the scanned graph is an error — spec drift; the scanned graph is the stronger check (resolves → real, planned → pending, gone → error). Materialized as an old-model DomainRule (product Invariant auto-created).

title: DriftIsError
body: 2.0 source §4.1: an implemented-by code FQN that is gone from the scanned graph is an error — spec drift; the scanned graph is the stronger check (resolves → real, planned → pending, gone → error). Materialized as an old-model DomainRule (product Invariant auto-created).

name: project-commands
body: 2.0-mapping (container kind app): the `apg project` command surface — `apg project start <name>` (§2.1) and `apg project merge` = verify gate → merge → main rebuild, binary-operated via git2 from the main checkout (§2.3). Proposed container; no code in the v0.10.4 graph.

name: mutation-guard
body: 2.0-mapping (container kind service — cross-cutting enforcement point): the project membership guard (§2.2) living in the central mutation funnel write_jsonl_and_reingest beside the staleness gate (§2.3), plus the pre-merge coherence gate behind the renamed `apg plan verify` (§2.2). One real-code anchor exists today: apg.artifacts.write_jsonl_and_reingest (src/artifacts.rs).

name: layers-serializer
body: 2.0-mapping (container kind app): the node-file serializer behind §3 (tier model, spine validation matrix) and §4 (apg/layers/ layout, one file per node, pairwise edges, atomic write-throughs, auto-commit). Proposed container; no code in the v0.10.4 graph.

name: plan-bridge
body: 2.0-mapping (container kind app): the transient tier-4 bridge (§5) — PlanPhase/Task/planned Implementation nodes live only in apg/.trans/plans/ per branch, never durable; plan mutations never commit; satisfies/gates/contains + Task→Implementation verbs (creates/modifies/deletes/renames/moves); feedback transient in .trans mirrors. Proposed container; no code in the v0.10.4 graph.

name: init-version-gate
body: 2.0-mapping (container kind app): `apg init` scaffolding apg/.worktrees/ + gitignore entry + binary-managed `version` in apg/config.json (§2.4), and the version gate (blocks not warns; missing version blocks; major/minor mismatch EITHER direction blocks; applies to apg scan + apg project start; init is the upgrade act). Proposed container; no code in the v0.10.4 graph.

name: projects
body: 2.0-mapping: synthetic old-model Subdomain forced by the strict Contains chain `Domain ⊃ Subdomain ⊃ Aggregate ⊃ Entity/ValueObject` (src/load.rs contains_pairs) — the 2.0 Group hierarchy is flat (groups in groups, §3.1). Hosts the project-context aggregate.

name: project-context
body: 2.0-mapping: synthetic old-model Aggregate (root Project) forced by the strict Contains chain `Domain ⊃ Subdomain ⊃ Aggregate ⊃ Entity/ValueObject` — 2.0 collapses aggregate specialness to behavior (§3.1: Group root attribute for aggregate-groups). Hosts entities Project/GraphNode + value-object NodeName: the change-set container and the graph nodes it carries (identity per §4.1).

name: Project
body: 2.0-mapping: source §2.1 — "project" is the change-set container created by `apg project start <name>`: a git worktree at <main>/apg/.worktrees/<project> on a branch named after the project (branch name == project name is the membership mechanism), off the repo's DEFAULT branch. Aggregate root entity (old model has no Entity kind field; plain Entity).

name: GraphNode
body: 2.0-mapping: source §3.1/§5 — every graph node the spec/plan/layers model touches: code nodes (scanned, never serialized) and tier-1–3 nodes (serialized one file per node under the 2.0 apg/layers/ tree). Old-model Entity standing in for the 2.0 universal "node" the serialization and pairwise-edge rules talk about (§4.1).

name: NodeName
body: 2.0-mapping: source §4.1 — a node's file name IS its identity; the 2.0 name allowlist [a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]* (refuse, never sanitize, §3.3). Old-model ValueObject standing in for 2.0 Value semantics (plain-name DDD, immutable; ValueObject here is the old-model type).

title: One-command project context creation
body: `apg project start <name>` creates the project context in one command: worktree + branch off the repo's DEFAULT branch (symbolic HEAD, not literal main) + auto-scan (worktree + branch + branch DB). Worktree location fixed at <main>/apg/.worktrees/<project>. Always a branch — no escape hatch, no --no-branch, no degradation. Idempotent ONLY when <name> matches the current project context (already in that project's worktree/branch → no-op, print the path); otherwise hard fail. AC: one command yields worktree + branch + branch DB. Source: plans/SPEC-apg-projects.md §2.1.

title: Hard refusals with case-specific fix lines
body: Hard refusals at project start: non-git dirs (suggest `apg init`); dirty main at start; unborn HEAD ("commit an initial state first"); invalid branch names NEVER sanitized (project names inherit git refname constraints); every collision is a case-specific "project already exists" — branch checked out elsewhere / branch without worktree / worktree dir present but not a worktree — naming the actual state and the fix command. `project start` is a main-checkout operation: run from inside a worktree → hard fail ("you work one project at a time"). AC: refusal exits 1 with a fix line. Source: plans/SPEC-apg-projects.md §2.1.

title: git2 plumbing, no git-CLI shell-outs
body: git2 crate with default-features = false (no https/ssh → no OpenSSL). The git CLI is never shelled out to; push/tag remain human acts. VI: cargo check and cargo test pass green with git2 default-features=false. Source: plans/SPEC-apg-projects.md §2.3.

title: Init scaffolds worktree dir + version field
body: `apg init` scaffolds apg/.worktrees/ + its gitignore entry and writes the binary version into apg/config.json as a binary-managed `version` field (user code_type rules untouched). `project start` self-heals the dir/gitignore if absent. Source: plans/SPEC-apg-projects.md §2.4.

title: One model per layer
body: One model per layer (2.0 catalog): requirements = Stakeholder/User/Requirement/Note/Constraint with the requirement tree at all depths (theme → epic → feature → story is ONE node type; spec-writer carries decomposition guidance — decompose until each requirement is atomic/testable); domain = Group/Entity/Value/Service/Note/Constraint; solution = System/Container/Component/Person/Note/Constraint; plans = the bridge, .trans-only; implementation = code — scanned, never serialized, Note/Constraint attach only; global = Constraint (the laws) + Notes. Source: plans/SPEC-apg-projects.md §3.1.

title: Sequential spine + write-time edge-kind validation
body: Spine strictly sequential — no tier skips (lint): Stakeholder ⊃ Requirement —Drives→ Domain —RealisedBy→ Solution —ImplementedBy→ code; User→domain role→Person is the same individual through the chain (represents edges); Person --uses--> System is same-tier C4, not a spine hop. Write-time edge-kind validation matrix (§3.3): contains (Stakeholder/User/Requirement→Requirement, Group→Group/Entity/Value/Service, System→Container, Container→Component), drives (Requirement→Domain), realised-by (Domain→Solution), implemented-by (Solution→code FQN validated vs scanned graph), calls/publishes/subscribes (Service↔Service / Service→Entity(kind event)), depends-on (Requirement→Requirement), uses (Person→System), represents (User→Entity, Entity→Person), details (Note→any). Node rules: name allowlist [a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]* — refuse, never sanitize; type must exist in its layer; Entity requires kind entity/event; Group takes core/supporting/generic + optional root; Container takes app/service/db/queue; FQN = <layer>.<type>.<name> for authored nodes (code nodes keep their language-native FQNs) — names unique per (layer, type); contains/depends-on trees acyclic; dangling FQN references are write-time errors. Source: plans/SPEC-apg-projects.md §3.2 + §3.3.

title: Coupling derived; constraints declarative over existing things
body: Coupling is DERIVED, never stored: A and B are coupled iff a service/event edge chain connects them. The DDD context-map flavors (direct / published / translated / shared / coevolving) are EDGE ATTRIBUTES on calls/publishes/subscribes — never node types, never Group→Group edges. Constraints are PROSE ("X must hold") over things that EXIST: the binary validates a constraint's structure and references at write time; global constraints guard the whole graph; local constraints attach to any tier-1–3 node (requirement AC, domain law, design bound); SATISFACTION IS ASSESSED BY REVIEW (non-deterministic), never executed — no constraint-expression language; a constraint is never a non-thing. Source: plans/SPEC-apg-projects.md §3.1 + §3.3.

title: Plans are the transient tier-4 bridge
body: Plans are tier 4 — the bridge. Plan nodes (PlanPhase, Task, planned Implementation nodes) exist ONLY in apg/.trans/plans/ per branch, never durable. Plan edges: contains (Plan ⊃ PlanPhase ⊃ Task), gates (PlanPhase→PlanPhase), satisfies (PlanPhase→Requirement). Task→Implementation verbs: creates (builds a planned node — FQN declared in the plan, not in the scanned graph), modifies (FQN must resolve in the scanned graph), deletes (FQN must resolve), renames / moves (FQN changes); further verbs reveal themselves through dogfooding. Feedback is transient — branch-lifecycle data, never committed; .trans mirrors the layers structure (feedback sits in the tier dir of its attached node); Reviews edges link feedback to durable nodes without polluting node files; review state dies with the branch, the reviewed nodes persist. Verification items are the plan's test tier (unit/int/e2e), not graph content. Source: plans/SPEC-apg-projects.md §5.

title: Bootstrap + dogfood operational flow
body: Standalone change-set + dogfood operational flow: the apg repo dogfoods the model — THIS spec is the bootstrap dogfood (authored with the v0.10.4 binary in the old model, within its boundaries; branch/worktree created manually because `apg project start` does not exist yet; from the next feature onward the binary handles it). Agent flow: the navigator runs `apg project start <name>` from the main checkout; the binary prints the worktree path; the navigator operates with cwd inside the worktree. Suite tools work unchanged — walk-up discovery finds the worktree's own apg/; opencode sessions are rooted at the repo, so the project session/tool workdir points at the worktree, not the main checkout. Test worktree apg/.worktrees/test stays until before shipping (the agent can see the verified pattern); cleanup deletes no branch. Source: plans/SPEC-apg-projects.md §6.

title: Membership guard — writes only, two-part failure UX
body: The project membership guard: guards WRITES only — reads are always allowed (queries/scans work anywhere; `project start` itself is unguarded, the entry point). Writes refuse outside a project context — the durable node/edge mutations (`apg node`/`apg edge`; the old spec/invariant/note writes are node/edge mutations here) and the transient plan/review mutations. Membership = "the project's worktree, on the project's branch": current branch == project name AND current checkout is the project's worktree (path under <main>/apg/.worktrees/<project>); failure messages name which half failed. Main is never a mutation place — delivered or not; post-merge changes are new change-sets. No "adoption" of legacy JSONLs (a spec on main just is; starting a project brings it along in the worktree). Universal-scope artifacts (e.g. global constraints) are authored from inside a project like any mutation — scope is orthogonal to mutation context. Error UX: exit 1; stderr = (1) which membership half failed, (2) one actionable fix line. AC: a failure names which half failed. Source: plans/SPEC-apg-projects.md §2.2.

title: Root resolution split (walk-up + git2 identity)
body: Root resolution split: keep the existing walk-up for checkout-local apg/ (correct in worktrees by construction); use git2 for identity (branch, checkout path, main path, worktree existence). Invariant: the git checkout root contains the apg/ the walk-up found — verify cheaply, error on divergence. Source: plans/SPEC-apg-projects.md §2.3.

title: Version gate blocks old layouts (scan + project start)
body: The version gate BLOCKS, never warns: same major.minor → proceed (patch diff fine); missing `version` (pre-versioning layout) → block; major or minor mismatch in EITHER direction → block with upgrade guidance. Applies to `apg scan` and `apg project start` (the layout-touching operations); `apg init` is the upgrade act. Upgrade instructions ship as a suite doc (~/.opencode/lib/apg-upgrade.md). Source: plans/SPEC-apg-projects.md §2.4.

title: Solution coverage by plan tasks, derived and enforced
body: Coverage is derived and enforced: every solution node's implemented-by FQN must be touched by at least one plan task. The plan is the HOW for the whole solution; the bridge is complete iff coverage holds. Source: plans/SPEC-apg-projects.md §5.

title: Guard in the central mutation funnel
body: The guard lives in the central mutation funnel — write_jsonl_and_reingest (src/artifacts.rs), beside the existing staleness gate: one check covers all mutations. Consequence: non-git test fixtures gain a real project context (real git fixtures with branch + worktree). Source cites "src/artifacts.rs:72"; the graph locates the function at lines 54–99 (start_line 54) — anchor FQN apg.artifacts.write_jsonl_and_reingest. Source: plans/SPEC-apg-projects.md §2.3.

title: Layers layout + file-name identity
body: Layout + identity: the SIX-layer catalog (requirements/domain/solution/plans/implementation/global) with storage policy separate from the catalog — plans serialize only under apg/.trans/plans/ (transient, per branch); implementation = the code (scanned, never serialized; attach-only note/constraint durable dir); the other four durable. apg/layers/ tree — requirements/{stakeholder,user,requirement,note,constraint}, domain/{group,entity,value,service,note,constraint}, solution/{system,container,component,person,note,constraint}, implementation/{note,constraint}, global/{constraint,note} — plus apg/.trans mirrors (plans per branch; feedback in the tier dir of the attached node, ALL six tiers incl. global). One file per node; the file name IS the identity: FQN = <layer>.<type>.<name> — no project prefix. Node-file schema: layer/type/name/body/properties/in/out, with the binary checking that layer/type/name match the path. Short ids (R1) may exist as metadata only, never as identity. Source: plans/SPEC-apg-projects.md §4.1.

title: No migration — old layouts re-materialized
body: No migration: legacy apg/specs/*.jsonl and apg/notes/ are NOT read; the version gate blocks old layouts; re-materialize instead. A migration would institutionalize the wrong model — the lossy mapping is the spec-writer's judgement, not a converter's. The old `apg spec` / `apg invariant` command surfaces and the old-model graph vocabulary are removed from the binary — node kinds are exactly the §3.1 catalog plus the code kinds and the transient plan/review kinds; edge kinds are exactly the §3.3 matrix plus the §5 plan/feedback edges; nothing else remains. VI: legacy specs unread — the binary never opens apg/specs/*.jsonl or apg/notes/. Source: plans/SPEC-apg-projects.md §4.1.

title: Plan apply → plan verify; project merge
body: `apg plan apply` is renamed `apg plan verify` — the binary applies nothing; verify is the pre-merge coherence gate (no remaining planned/dangling nodes + all feedback resolved), guarded (a verdict is only meaningful against the branch's graph). `apg project merge` = verify gate → merge → main rebuild: binary-operated via git2 from the main checkout — the project's terminal lifecycle act; the rebuild is a plain unguarded scan on main. Source: plans/SPEC-apg-projects.md §2.2 + §2.3.

title: Pairwise edges + atomic write-throughs + code exemption
body: Edge pairing + atomic write-throughs: BOTH in and out edges live in the node file (out in the source's file, in in the target's). Validation: an in/out edge in one file without the matching out/in edge in the other endpoint's file is an ERROR, caught at ingestion (AC); a match = same source, kind, target, AND edge properties; outgoing edges are canonical for building the graph. Transient-to-durable relationships stay ENTIRELY in .trans — both halves recorded there referencing durable node FQNs; committed node files never hold transient references; ingestion combines and validates the pairs. Code endpoints are EXEMPT from the pairwise rule — code nodes have no files: the implemented-by edge is recorded on the spec side only, as a code FQN, validated against the scanned graph — resolves → real; planned (in .trans) → pending, not an error; gone from the scanned graph → error (spec drift); the scanned graph is the stronger check. Renames/deletions are atomic write-throughs: rename = file move + FQN change + rewrite of every referencing file; delete = file removal + rewrite of incident edges out of referencing files; ONE LOGICAL MUTATION updates ALL affected files and commits once — complete validation before anything is written, restore the previous state on failure (never leave mismatched endpoint files). Source: plans/SPEC-apg-projects.md §4.1.

title: Graph mutations auto-commit (plans never)
body: Graph mutations auto-commit on the project branch via git2: one commit per logical mutation — all affected files together (single-file diffs when a mutation touches one file). Codebase changes are committed by the implementer (unchanged agent flow). After an auto-commit the staleness gate's recorded scan_meta is re-anchored (DB and tree in sync by construction). Plan mutations NEVER commit — .trans is gitignored and transient; branch commits carry only code + node files. Source: plans/SPEC-apg-projects.md §2.3 + §4.2.
R1 (§2.1): one `apg project start <name>` command yields the worktree + branch + branch DB — the branch DB exists after start.
R2 (§2.1): every hard-refusal case exits 1 with a fix line on stderr naming the actual state and the command that fixes it.
R3 (§2.2): a refused mutation's error names which membership half failed (branch half vs worktree half) plus one actionable fix line.
R6 (§2.3): cargo check and cargo test pass green with the git2 crate at default-features = false.
R17 (§4.1): legacy specs unread — the binary never opens apg/specs/*.jsonl or apg/notes/ (only the layers layout), verified by inspection + the version-gate blocking an old layout.

No migration tooling (§4.1): legacy apg/specs/*.jsonl and apg/notes/ are never read and no converter is built — the lossy mapping is the spec-writer's judgement, not a converter's; re-materialize instead.
No Decision node type (§1.5): decisions are not modeled — the endstate (code/structure) is the record; explanations the structure doesn't carry become notes. (Not even in the 2.0 model.)
No APG_NO_PROJECT_GUARD escape hatch — of any kind (§2.3): reads are unguarded, so tooling never needs to mutate outside a project.
No per-type CLI subcommands (§3.1): the node-type catalog is data over the generic mutation path, not a CLI surface per type.
No configurable worktree location (§2.1): the worktree location is fixed at <main>/apg/.worktrees/<project> — a gitignored path inside the main checkout, tested and verified safe.

No stored Group→Group coupling edges (§3.1/§3.3): coupling is derived, never stored; the DDD context-map flavors (direct/published/translated/shared/coevolving) are edge attributes on calls/publishes/subscribes.

The five governing principles of the source (§1): (1) a project is a container for a change-set over the graph (and the code that underpins the implementation graph) — a project ≠ a spec ≠ a plan, it CONTAINS those things; (2) no-spoon — it is not possible to mutate the graph without a project, at all; projects are ephemeral change-set containers; the nodes are the reality; (3) serialize nodes, not specs — one file per node, no project segment anywhere in the path; present-ness is branch membership of the file; (4) merge-conflict localization is the goal — different change-sets touching different nodes never collide on a file; the same node edited by two change-sets conflicts at that node, a meaningful conflict; (5) the endstate is the thing we care about — decisions are not modeled, the code/structure is the record; explanations the structure doesn't carry become notes. plans/SPEC-apg-projects.md §1.

Principle 2, "no spoon" (§1.2): "It is not possible to mutate the graph without a project — at all." Projects are ephemeral change-set containers; the nodes are the reality. A spec/plan/review JSONL on main means only that there is a spec in the graph — it is not a project and carries no project semantics.

Worktree safety (§2.1): the fixed worktree location <main>/apg/.worktrees/<project> is a gitignored path INSIDE the main checkout — tested and verified safe; gitignored paths are not part of the worktree. The apg repo dogfoods the pattern: test worktree apg/.worktrees/test stays until before shipping (the agent can see the verified pattern); cleanup deletes no branch (§6).

2.0 rationale (§3.1): the domain layer takes DDD semantics with PLAIN names because DDD nomenclature is cryptic — Group (BoundedContext/Subdomain/Aggregate/DomainRule all collapse into it), Entity, Value, Service. This bootstrap spec still uses old-model DDD type names (domain/subdomain/aggregate/entity/value-object/domain-event/domain-rule) because they are the only types the v0.10.4 binary knows; the plain-name catalog is requirements R11/R12 and the future layers-serializer's data model.

"The endstate is the record" (§1.5): decisions are not modeled — the code/structure is the record. Accordingly, NO Decision nodes are authored in this spec even though the old model supports them; explanations the structure doesn't carry become notes (this note and its siblings are those explanations). The 2.0 model keeps this: non-goal "no Decision node type".

Coupling is derived, never stored (§3.1/§3.3): A and B are coupled iff a service/event edge chain connects them; the DDD context-map flavors (direct/published/translated/shared/coevolving) are edge attributes on calls/publishes/subscribes, never node types and never Group→Group edges. Carried by R14 and the non-goal "no stored Group→Group coupling edges".

Constraints are declarative ("X must hold") over things that EXIST (§3.1): global constraints guard the whole graph and are checked at every scan; local constraints attach to any tier-1–3 node (a requirement AC, a domain law, a design bound); a constraint is never a non-thing. In this bootstrap spec the domain laws are materialized as old-model DomainRules (MutationRequiresProject, PairwiseEdgeMatching, PlanCoversSolution, DriftIsError).

Bootstrap context (§6): this change-set is standalone — the cosanima 1.0 spec is deleted and, when it returns, re-materializes on its own branch as its own project. This spec is authored with the current binary (v0.10.4) in the OLD model, within its boundaries, and will be re-materialized in the new (2.0) model later; the new model is the shape the binary ships toward and the version gate blocks the layout switch (§2.4). This session is the bootstrap dogfood: branch/worktree created manually because `apg project start` does not exist yet; from the next feature onward the binary handles it.

source: §3.1/§4.1/§6 describe the 2.0 model — five layers under apg/layers/, one file per node, FQN = layer.name with no project prefix, legacy apg/specs/*.jsonl + apg/notes/ unread; inconsistency: the v0.10.4 bootstrap binary supports only the OLD model — one spec project per JSONL under apg/specs/, old node types (Requirement/Phase/NonGoal/AcceptanceCriterion/VerificationItem/Note + DDD/C4 kinds), no layers tree, no version gate; resolution: represent the 2.0 source with old-model types in the bootstrap spec project `apg-projects`; R9/R10/R17 state the 2.0 init/version-gate/layout the binary ships toward; re-materialization in the new model is the planned follow-up (§6) and the lossy mapping is this spec-writer's judgement [autonomous]

source: §3.1 — one flat domain layer: Group (hierarchical; core/supporting/generic + root for aggregate-groups; BoundedContext/Subdomain/Aggregate/DomainRule all collapse into it; aggregate specialness behavioral), Entity kind entity|event, Value immutable, Service stateless; inconsistency: old-model DDD has no Group type and enforces a STRICT Contains chain `Domain ⊃ Subdomain ⊃ Aggregate ⊃ Entity/ValueObject` (src/load.rs contains_pairs) — flat hierarchies, Entity kind fields and DomainRule-collapse are not representable; resolution: mapped 2.0 concepts onto old-model types — Domain change-sets; SYNTHETIC Subdomain projects (core) + Aggregate project-context (root Project) because old-model Entities cannot hang directly under a Domain; Entity Project (the change-set container, §2.1) and Entity GraphNode (the universal graph node, §3.1/§5) + ValueObject NodeName (2.0 Value: file-name identity, §4.1); 2.0 events (Entity kind=event) → DomainEvent nodes ProjectStarted / NodeFileWritten; 2.0 domain laws/constraints → DomainRule nodes MutationRequiresProject / PairwiseEdgeMatching / PlanCoversSolution / DriftIsError, each also materializing a product Invariant [autonomous]

source: §3.2/§3.3 — spine strictly sequential (Stakeholder ⊃ Requirement —Drives→ Domain —RealisedBy→ Solution —ImplementedBy→ code), no tier skips (lint), write-time edge-kind validation matrix; inconsistency: old-model spine verbs (Drives/Requires/Realises/Represents/ImplementedBy) are permissive — no sequential-spine lint and no write-time edge-kind matrix exist in the v0.10.4 binary; resolution: threaded every requirement --drives→ domain.change-sets and domain.change-sets --represents→ system.apg-cli; the 2.0 validation matrix and sequential-spine rule are carried as requirement text (R13) to be enforced by the future binary, not as enforced graph properties of this bootstrap spec [autonomous]

source: §5 — the 2.0 spec carries NO phase structure; plans (PlanPhase) carry phases in .trans; inconsistency: the old model requires spec phases with Gates edges (Spec ⊃ Phase, Gates chains); resolution: authored old-model phases 1..5 — projects-model → init-version-gate → serialization-model → plans-transient → rollout — chained by Gates (2←1, 3←2, 4←3, 5←4) as a bootstrap-only representation of the source's five-part shape; requirements are grouped by --feature (the source's own grouping) since the old model does not attach requirements to phases; the 2.0 phase-in-plans semantics are carried by R18 [autonomous]

source: §4.1 — the file name IS the identity; FQN = <layer>.<type>.<name>, no project prefix; short ids (R1) may exist as metadata only, never as identity; inconsistency: old-model FQNs are project-scoped (<project>/spec.R1, <project>/<kind>.<name>) and the short ids R1..R20 ARE the identity of this bootstrap spec's requirements; resolution: requirements keep old-model project-scoped FQNs with short ids as identity for the bootstrap; the 2.0 identity rule is stated verbatim in R15 and will be enforced by the future layers-serializer container [autonomous]

source: §3.1 — a requirement AC is a LOCAL CONSTRAINT attached to the tier-1–3 node; §5 — verification items are the plan's test tier (unit/int/e2e), never graph content; inconsistency: old-model AcceptanceCriterion/VerificationItem nodes hang under the spec root with no attachment edge to any requirement; resolution: authored AC nodes for R1/R2/R3 and VI nodes for R6/R17 with the requirement id in the body (the AC/VI statements also stay inline in the requirement bodies, matching the source summary verbatim); the 2.0 test-tier verification semantics are carried by R18 [autonomous]

source: the 2.0 source never names a System or Containers — it speaks of "the binary" (§2.3) and command surfaces (`apg project start` §2.1, `apg project merge` §2.3, `apg plan verify` §2.2, `apg init` §2.4, the layers serializer §4, the plan bridge §5); inconsistency: the old model requires a C4 tree (System ⊃ Container ⊃ Component) for tier-3 nodes and pending anchors; resolution: named the System apg-cli with five proposed Containers — project-commands (kind app), mutation-guard (kind service: the cross-cutting enforcement point), layers-serializer (kind app), plan-bridge (kind app), init-version-gate (kind app) — all pending anchors; container kinds are this spec-writer's judgement; the one real-code mapping today is mutation-guard --implemented-by→ apg.artifacts.write_jsonl_and_reingest, which is also R4's resolved anchor [autonomous]

DependsOn mis-aimed: R8 (auto-commit "on the project branch via git2") consumes R5 (plan apply→verify rename + `project merge`), but §2.3's own ordering puts auto-commit BEFORE the merge act, and the merge is the *consumer* of auto-committed branch state — not a prerequisite of it. Meanwhile R8's real prereqs are unlinked: the git2 crate (R6, same feature) and the git2-based identity/root split (R7) must exist before any git2 auto-commit can land. As authored, a plan-writer ordering tasks topologically over DependsOn can schedule R8 before R6/R7 with no edge preventing it. Fix: re-point R8 to consume R6 (and optionally R7); drop R8→R5 (R5's chain R5→R4→R3→R1 stands). Source: plans/SPEC-apg-projects.md §2.3 + §4.2.

Non-goal has no source basis: "No per-type CLI subcommands (§3.1)" — the source's §3.1 is a node-type catalog (table + plain-name semantics) and never states anything about a CLI surface, per-type subcommands, or a "generic mutation path" (searched the full source; the only CLI statements are §2.3's "the git CLI is never shelled out to" and §6's operational flow). Every other non-goal (ng-1/2/3/5/6) maps to an explicit source sentence; this one is an undocumented inference — and it sits oddly against the current binary, which *does* expose per-type `apg spec add <kind>` subcommands. Since non-goals bind what the plan-writer excludes, either cite the source sentence it derives from, annotate it as writer judgement (the note-9..16 pattern), or drop it. Source: plans/SPEC-apg-projects.md §3.1 (no such statement).

Source statement with no graph trace: §3.1 defines Stakeholder ("anyone with an interest — 'a thing that has an opinion'") alongside User, but only the User half is captured (R12 carries "User ⊂ Stakeholder ('a thing that uses the system')"); the Stakeholder definition appears in no requirement body, domain/solution node, or note (notes 1-8 summarize §1/§3.1 rationale but not the tier-1 definitions). Since R11/R12 are the requirements carrying the 2.0 layer catalog for the future layers-serializer, the definitional gap leaves the requirements-layer semantics half-specified. Fix: add the Stakeholder clause to R12 (next to the User clause it already carries). Source: plans/SPEC-apg-projects.md §3.1 ("Requirements:" paragraph, line 114).

Anchor/container-scope inconsistency: R5 bundles two surfaces — the plan-verify rename (pre-merge coherence gate) and `apg project merge` (verify → merge → main rebuild, binary-operated via git2 from the main checkout). It anchors only to container.mutation-guard, whose 2.0-mapping body covers the verify gate — but container project-commands' own body (note-16) claims `apg project merge` (§2.3) as part of ITS command surface. R4 already demonstrates the straddling pattern (resolved code anchor + pending container anchor); R5's merge half is under-expressed by a single mutation-guard anchor, so a plan-writer filing tasks by anchor will hang the merge command off the wrong container. Fix: add a second pending anchor to container.project-commands (or re-anchor). Source: plans/SPEC-apg-projects.md §2.2 + §2.3.

source: feedback-2 — ng-4's body cites "(§3.1)", but the source's §3.1 (plans/SPEC-apg-projects.md) is a node-type catalog (table + plain-name semantics) and never states anything about a CLI surface, per-type subcommands, or a generic mutation path; the only CLI statements in the source are §2.3 (the git CLI is never shelled out to) and §6's operational flow; inconsistency: ng-4's §3.1 citation is unbacked, unlike ng-1/2/3/5/6 which map to explicit source sentences; resolution: retained ng-4 — the boundary is real, user-confirmed in the design discussion that produced the source (the navigator's CLI scaffold: one `apg node`/`apg edge` mutation surface with the node type as an argument — no per-type subcommands, the pattern the old-model `apg spec add <kind>` surface follows), and the source implies the generic node/edge mutation path: §3.3's write-time type-in-layer validation matrix and §4.1's `layer/<type>/<name>` layout treat type as data over one mutation path, and §4.2 says "each node/edge mutation writes its file(s)"; non-goal bodies are append-only through the spec CLI (no edit path), so this note is the durable provenance + citation correction: read the body's §3.1 cite as shorthand for the design-scaffold decision and the §3.3/§4.1-implied generic surface [autonomous]

title: Domain + solution node semantics
body: Domain semantics use PLAIN names (DDD nomenclature is cryptic): Group hierarchical (groups in groups), attributes core/supporting/generic + root (root for aggregate-groups); BoundedContext/Subdomain/Aggregate/DomainRule all collapse into Group — aggregate specialness is behavioral and lives in implementation, not structure. Entity kind entity|event (events are ephemeral entities with motion, not a type). Value immutable. Service stateless behaviour. Container kind app/service/db/queue. Solution = C4 only; Person is the C4 view of User/Stakeholder (same individual, solution-side vocabulary); Stakeholder = anyone with an interest (""a thing that has an opinion""); User ⊂ Stakeholder (""a thing that uses the system""). Source: plans/SPEC-apg-projects.md §3.1.

Observed defect in the OLD model (this change-set's bootstrap): a requirement body-upsert (apg spec add upsert by FQN, used to fix review feedback-3 on R12) silently dropped incident edges — the outgoing Drives edge AND the incoming Reviews edge from feedback-3 — while rewriting the node record. The Drives edge was caught and restored immediately; the Reviews edge was not, and no writer-side tool can author Reviews edges (only `apg review add` writes Record::Reviews), leaving a deadlocked repair. This is exactly the failure the 2.0 atomic write-through (this requirement, §4.1) must prevent: a node rewrite must preserve/rewrite ALL incident edges (per the in/out-edge node-file model), never drop them silently. Regression target for the implementer: a spec-node edit must leave every incident edge intact.
